A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same MPG-SAM 2 work, with matching main-text methods, experiments, figures and tables. However, both end with references: v1's referenced loss-details appendix and v2's referenced parameter-analysis appendix are not included, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original MPG-SAM 2 benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative segmentation comparisons in Section 4, Tables 1–4 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and qualitative results and reports additional loss, prompting and memory ablations in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Equation 3 change the specified mask-prior output from sigmoid(MLP(Vg)) to MLP(Vg); Figure 2 also removes the sigmoid. This is a localized procedural revision. The expanded similarity-loss description documents a component already included in v1's training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ref-YouTube-VOS, Ref-DAVIS17 and MeViS for RVOS evaluation, with the same RefCOCO/+/g pretraining coverage. The new ablations vary model controls within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds VD-IT and VISA to the Ref-YouTube-VOS/Ref-DAVIS17 comparison in Table 1 and VISA to the MeViS comparison in Table 2. Existing comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: Tables 3–4 add controls without the similarity loss, with first-frame-only prompting, and without SAM 2 memory. The retained benchmark splits, evaluation metrics, backbones, image resolutions and training schedules are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests isolating the similarity loss, per-frame prompting and memory, plus a short resource-overhead analysis. Existing MPG/HGA component, attention-mode, patch-size and global-feature ablations remain, as do the qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds comparator scores, ablation results and resource estimates. Table 2 changes DsHmp's MeViS F from 39.8 to 49.8, consistent with its retained J=43.0 and J&F=46.4. New controls report J&F values of 69.4, 59.0 and 66.2; v1's 70.3 row remains explicitly marked as including Lsim, rather than declining to 69.4. MPG-SAM 2's headline scores remain 73.9, 72.4 and 53.7.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.6 adds explicit cosine-similarity and pixelwise MSE definitions for Lsim in Equations 5–6; v1 only names this loss and references an unavailable appendix. Equation 3 also removes the sigmoid. Other attention-equation simplifications largely restate retained operations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting SAM 2 through mask priors and hierarchical global-historical aggregation, improving temporal consistency and outperforming RVOS comparators. The additional evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an argument that BEiT-3's small 14×14 embedding grid makes global attention's computational and memory overhead acceptable. It also explains the baseline through per-frame prompting and memory. Existing temporal-consistency and patch-size interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 details the existing similarity loss through sentence projection, cosine similarities and pixelwise MSE. It newly reports MPG/HGA overhead of 21M parameters and memory stated as 1.3G. Main hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged; the promised detailed parameter appendix is unavailable.

R1.justification: VISA and VD-IT are newly cited, with a related-work discussion of VD-IT's use of video diffusion models. The introduction also qualifies its previously categorical criticism of RefSAM's semantic alignment. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Much of Sections 3.2–3.5 is substantially rewritten or condensed, including replacing explicit aggregator equations with prose. The introduction and results discussion are also revised, and Section 3.6 gains a dedicated loss explanation. This is extensive editorial revision despite retaining the section hierarchy.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is comprehensively redrawn with different module placement, connections and labels; Figure 3 is restyled. Tables 1–4 gain rows, a loss column, highlighting and placement changes. Figure 2 introduces an apparent error by labeling the mask-decoder block 'SAM 2 Prompt Encoder'; Figures 1 and 4 retain their content.

improvement.justification: The additional controls in Tables 3–4 improve component attribution, the expanded comparisons provide broader context, and the DsHmp correction resolves an internally inconsistent result. The existing similarity loss also becomes more inspectable. These limited gains outweigh the new Figure 2 labeling error, although missing referenced appendices still limit completeness. Unchanged headline scores do not establish a performance improvement.
